sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Indian River County?
sections.html:
Three county offices split the work. The Property Appraiser values property and takes exemption applications, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the county Value Adjustment Board hears appeals. Recorded deeds are kept by the Clerk of the Court.

The Property Appraiser keeps two offices: the Vero office at 1800 27th St., Bldg. B, Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469, and a Sebastian office at 1921 U.S. 1, (772) 226-1133, both open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. The Tax Collector's tax department answers at (772) 226-1343. Its own page says the office has no control over a property's assessed value or the amount of tax due.

The Tax Collector's site links to the county's municipalities, which include Vero Beach, Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Orchid and Fellsmere. A house in any of them sits on the same county tax collector's roll.

sections.h2: How large is the Indian River County tax roll?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser's home page reports a 2026 certified roll with $51,957,635,233 in just value and $33,819,841,085 in taxable value. It counts 96,241 real parcels and 9,853 tangible personal property accounts.

The gap between just value and taxable value reflects exemptions, assessment caps and other reductions. For a single parcel, the figures that matter are on your own notice: market value, assessed value and taxable value.

sections.h2: When are Indian River County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector mails bills by November 1. The discount steps down month by month, and gross tax is due in March.

  • 4% off if the payment is postmarked in November
  • 3% in December
  • 2% in January
  • 1% in February
  • No discount in March

The office says discounts follow the postmark. If no bill arrives by November 9, call the Tax Collector, because a missing bill does not excuse payment: state law makes the owner responsible for seeing that a bill is received. Send a written address change to the Property Appraiser, and expect a separate bill for each parcel you own.

Two bill messages deserve attention. A "Do Not Pay" notice means a mortgage company has requested your original bill, and "Back Taxes Remain Unpaid" means delinquent tax also sits on the account. Call (772) 226-1343 to learn the amount.

sections.h2: What happens if Indian River County property tax is not paid?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid on April 1 pick up a 3% penalty on the gross tax. Accounts still unpaid in May are charged an advertising fee and advertised once a week in a local newspaper for three consecutive weeks. A tax certificate must be sold on or before June 1.

The Tax Collector sends interested bidders to a county page on a tax certificate sale website. A certificate is a first lien against the property, and the holder can apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the issue year. When that happens, the Clerk runs the sale, with a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is larger, due with full payment within 24 hours.

The Tax Collector also states that it cannot accept partial payments on current or delinquent real estate tax bills. If you cannot pay the whole amount, the options are the installment plan for a later year, a homestead deferral if you qualify, or a sale that pays the tax from proceeds.

sections.h2: Can I pay Indian River County property tax in installments?
sections.html:
Yes, if next year's estimated bill is more than $100, but you must apply before the year the plan starts. Applications for the 2026 tax year are accepted from November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and the office stopped taking 2025 applications on May 1, 2026.

The plan has four bills: June with a 6% discount, September with 4.5%, December with 3%, and March with no discount. The June and September amounts use the prior year's tax, and December and March carry the adjustment to the actual new-year bill. The first payment is due in June, and Florida law allows a July payment without the 6% discount. If you miss June entirely, you drop off the plan and receive an ordinary November bill.

Payments outside the month due lose their discount, and the office cannot accept an installment in any other month. Selling mid-plan has a specific rule: the account stays on the plan for that year, so tell the closing agent which installments have been paid. A buyer who does not want the plan next year can ask the Tax Collector to remove the account.

sections.h2: What deferral and exemptions are available in Indian River County?
sections.html:
Homestead owners who qualify by age and income can defer part or all of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector on or before March 31. Interest is charged on deferred tax and treated as a lien, and the tax and interest come due on your death, on a sale of the home, or when the homestead status changes.

Homestead applications go to the Property Appraiser by March 1, and permanent Florida residency is required on January 1. The home page notes that applications submitted after September 6 count for the 2027 tax year, so a late 2026 filer waits for the following roll. The state's $50,000 exemption has two tiers: the first $25,000 applies to all taxes and the second applies only to non-school taxes on value above $50,000.

The state's Save Our Homes cap, at 2.7 percent for 2026, limits growth on a homestead. A sale resets the value to market level the following January 1, which is why a buyer's bill can differ from yours.

sections.h2: How do I contest my Indian River County assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board by the date printed on your Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which Florida sets at 25 days after the notices are mailed.

The Property Appraiser's home page links to the county's Value Adjustment Board site. If the appraiser denied an exemption, the state allows a petition 30 days after the denial letter is mailed. Bring comparable sales, photographs and repair estimates with you.

sections.h2: What should an Indian River County seller do about tax at closing?
sections.html:
Order a payoff, confirm which year's bill is open, and have the closing agent prorate it. The Tax Collector states the buyer is responsible for the whole November bill, but it is normally prorated at closing so the seller credits the buyer for the months of ownership. No money goes from the seller to the Tax Collector as a partial payment.

  • Check for a back-taxes message on the account.
  • Confirm any installment payments already made.
  • Ask whether deferred tax is attached to a homestead lien.
  • Check the recorded deeds at the Clerk's office.

Florida's deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party to the document is liable for it. A sale with back tax, a deferral lien or a damaged roof can be completed with a cash buyer who accepts the house as-is and has the title company pay what is owed.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Indian River County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the county tax payment portal the Tax Collector links from its site. Discounts follow the postmark date, and the tax department at (772) 226-1343 can tell you about other payment options.

faqs.q: When does Indian River County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. A 3% penalty is added to the gross tax, and unpaid accounts are advertised in May before the certificate sale on or before June 1.

faqs.q: When can I apply for the 2026 tax year installment plan?
faqs.a: The office accepts applications for the 2026 tax year from November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027. The April 30 deadline is firm, and the first payment falls in June.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of an Indian River County bill?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Collector states it cannot accept partial payments on current or delinquent real estate bills outside the installment plan.

faqs.q: Do I owe the whole year's tax if I sell in spring?
faqs.a: The owner when the bill is mailed receives it, but the closing agent normally prorates the year so the buyer reimburses the seller for the part after closing. Confirm the split on the closing statement.
